audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: verbatim in the held Nugteren 2011 text (held under dong1285/src, not linked to this record), sec 1.5.1.1 p.35; sec 2.4.3 p.63 supports it. (2) Deciding source is a 2011 comparative-historical LOT dissertation summarising the QG group, not a primary description of Bonan; Glottolog lists two modern reference grammars (Fried 2010, 348 pp, Tongren; Li Hao 2022, 326 pp, Gansu) that outrank it for this language. (3) Li Hao 2022 fetched sources from HAL: sec 2.1.7.1 p.57 states final-syllable accent (higher pitch, greater intensity, longer), predictable and non-distinctive, shifting onto suffixes; longer compounds keep per-lexeme accent; Mandarin loans carry contrastive pitch accents. This confirms 'fixed-dominant' final (rule 01 001 0001..., strict=false) and matches the compound/loan exceptions already in the record. SPP 58 (Chuluu 1994) fetched sources, silent on placement. Fried 2010, Li 1986 a

sources.citation: Nugteren 2011, Mongolic Phonology and the Gansu-Qinghai Languages, secs 1.5.1.1 and 2.4.3 (lotpublications.nl/Documents/, full PDF re-read)
sources.quote: Word-final accent is shared by all QG languages. [...] In Baoan most exceptions involve compounds, which apparently carried the main accent on the last syllable of the first member [...] Loanwords from Arabic may have non-final accent.

sources.citation: Li, Hao. 2022. Grammaire descriptive de la langue bao'an — perspectives comparatives dans l'aire linguistique du Gansu-Qinghai. Thèse de doctorat, INALCO (NNT 2022INAL0016), HAL tel-04009089, 326 pp.
sources.quote: 'Dans la langue bao'an du Gansu, l'accent se rencontre sur la dernière syllabe (oxyton) ... celle-ci se réalise par un son plus élevé (hauteur), plus fort (intensité) et plus long (durée). L'accent en bao'an est prévisible au niveau phonologique, mais il ne possède pas de valeur distinctive. Il apparait en général sur la syllabe finale, et l'accent déplace automatiquement lorsqu'un suffixe est adjoint à un lexème' (ex. 51 'rə / rə'tɕi / rətɕi'si); same for short compounds (52), but longer compounds keep an accent on each lexeme (53); sec 2.1.7.3: Mandarin loans carry two contrastive pitch acce
sources.locator: sec 2.1.7.1 'Accent du bao'an du Gansu', p.57 (PDF p.59); sec 2.1.7.2-2.1.7.3 pp.58-59 (scanned of p.57; text layer is font-shifted)
sources.note: Primary descriptive grammar (Gansu variety) with a dedicated accent section (2.1.7, pp.57-60) giving placement, correlates, suffix shift and compound behaviour; our coding rests on a group-level sentence in a comparative-historical monograph. fetched sources now; confirms final fixed-dominant.
